name: Donn

attributes.attribute: resided at Tech Duinn, a rocky island off southwest Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donn is the Irish god of the dead. His name puns the words for "brown" and "king." He appears in few myths. People often confused him with other mythological figures. He lived at Tech Duinn, the House of Donn. This rocky island stood off the southwest coast of Ireland. He also connected to Donn Well in County Donegal. People conflated him with the Dagda, the god of abundance. The two shared only a home in the Otherworld. Donn stood for isolation and death. He caused death by drowning. From his seaside home he brewed storms to sink ships. The storms drew more souls to his realm.
objective: Records Donn, the shadowy Irish god of the dead, his home at Tech Duinn, and his association with drowning.
key_results: Donn is the Irish god of the dead.
He lived at Tech Duinn, the House of Donn, on a rocky island off southwest Ireland.
He had a further connection to Donn Well in County Donegal.
People conflated him with the Dagda; both lived in the Otherworld but had little in common.
He brewed storms to cause shipwrecks and draw souls to his realm.
